newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns against BA/AA slot-selling.
newsitem.headline: EU warns against BA/AA slot-selling.

text.p: European Union sources warned on Monday that the European Commission still had "serious doubts" about whether to clear the alliance between American Airlines and BA, adding that recent suggestions of slot-selling made things worse.

"Selling slots is not something we can accept. It's not legal," one source said, referring to a British government statement that it would clear the alliance if the two companies met certain conditions including giving up 168 landing slots at London Heathrow airport.
British Airways responded that it would divest of slots only "on the basis of fair market value".

The EU sources said dropping the slots would not compensate for the alliance's possible threat to competition, that the companies should cede more than 168 slots and that they should give them away rather than sell them.
They also strongly argued that the Commission had competence to rule on the alliance announced earlier this year, despite suggestions that the British and U.S. authorities had sole jurisdiction.
"We have our own jurisdiction and we are going to apply it," one source said, adding that the Commission hoped for good cooperation with the national antitrust authorities.

In October, the Commission sent BA and AA a so-called "statement of objections" outlining its concerns about the deal. The companies are expected to reply by January, after which the Commission could organise a hearing with all interested parties.

EU sources noted that on certain British-U.S. destinations the companies would control a large proportion of the passenger traffic -- for example, 83 percent on the London-Chicago route and 78 percent on the London-New York Kennedy Airport route, the sources said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
